meta.title: Ukrainian Alphabet
meta.subtitle: 33 letters and the apostrophe · both directions, as two cards per letter
meta.desc: The 33 letters of the Ukrainian alphabet, in alphabetical order, and the apostrophe — the first deck of the Ukrainian collection, since the level decks are written in Cyrillic from their first card and carry no transliteration. Both directions: see a letter and recall its sound, or see a sound and recall the letter, each a card with its own schedule. Every note gives the letter in capital and small, its name (what a Ukrainian calls it when spelling a word aloud), its sound described in English words, and one everyday word that shows it, with its stress marked and a speaker beside it. The sounds are approximations, as every learner's alphabet gives them; where English has no near equivalent, as for и, the rolled р and х, the card says so. Four things a reader who knows Russian should unlearn are on the cards: г is a voiced h and ґ is the g; и and і are two different vowels; е is never "ye" (є is); and an unstressed о is still said as o. The soft sign ь and the apostrophe have no sound of their own, and their cards say what they do instead.

fields.Name: ве
fields.Sound: "v" as in van; at the end of a syllable, nearer the w of how

fields.Name: ге
fields.Sound: a voiced "h", like the h of ahead said with the voice on — never the g of go

fields.Name: ґе
fields.Sound: "g" as in go; a letter of few words

fields.Name: є
fields.Sound: "ye" as in yes; after a consonant, "e" with the consonant softened

fields.Name: и
fields.Sound: a short vowel near the i of bit, said a little further back; not the same as і

fields.Name: ї
fields.Sound: "yee" as in yeast — always a y and an i

fields.Name: йот
fields.Sound: "y" as in boy — a short i, always beside a vowel

fields.Name: о
fields.Sound: "o" as in more, but shorter — and still o when unstressed

fields.Name: ер
fields.Sound: a rolled "r", made with the tip of the tongue; English has no equivalent

fields.Name: ха
fields.Sound: "kh", like the ch in Scottish loch

fields.Name: ща
fields.Sound: "shch", the sh and ch of fresh cheese said together

fields.Name: мʼяки́й знак
fields.Sound: the soft sign: no sound of its own; it softens the consonant before it

fields.Name: ю
fields.Sound: "yu" as in you; after a consonant, "u" with the consonant softened

fields.Name: апостро́ф
fields.Sound: the apostrophe, not a letter: no sound of its own; before я, ю, є or ї it keeps the consonant hard and lets their y be heard
